methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Shinkei, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Saif Khawaja and Reed Ginsberg, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set spanning 9 private peers and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Series B companies Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), alongside earlier-stage peers like Walden Robotics ($1.1B).

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement to the $30M raised proxy, implying a $60M valuation. Peer-median analysis, based on the 4-peer cohort of same-sector and same/adjacent-stage companies, yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The divergence reflects the maturity spread within the peer set, which includes later-stage Series B companies alongside a Seed-stage entry point.

Triangulating both methods across 2 approaches produces a low of $51M, a median of $880M, and a high of $2.0B. The wide band reflects material uncertainty around growth trajectory and comparability across stages. The peer-median method carries particular weight given direct sector alignment, though the Series B concentration in the peer set may inflate projections for a Series A company. Stage-progression analysis, conversely, relies on typical multipliers rather than company-specific fundamentals. Revenue traction, market size capture, and burn efficiency would materially narrow this range.
